blocks.text: 1. Agentic RAG
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721031-751867040.png

Graph RAG closed by weighing when its graph construction effort is worth it. Agentic RAG, where retrieval is driven by an autonomous agent making its own decisions, closes out the Advanced RAG module and previews the dedicated Agentic RAG module covered later in this course.
It lets an agent decide what to retrieve, when to retrieve, and when the task is actually done, an autonomous decision making process explored in full throughout this topic.
2. Fixed Pipeline Versus Agent Decisions
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721031-541320206.png
A fixed pipeline, like the four stage pipeline covered in Naive RAG, runs the same stages in the same order for every query.
An agent instead decides at each step what action to take next.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Architecture","How the next step is chosen"],"rows":[["Fixed pipeline","Same stages in the same order, every query"],["Agentic RAG","Agent decides the next action at each step"]]}

blocks.text: 3. The Agent Calls Tools Not Just A Retriever

blocks.alt: The Agent Calls Tools Not Just A Retriever
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721032-215627610.png
Beyond a single vector retriever, an agentic system can call a web search tool, a calculator, or a database query.
Retrieval becomes just one tool among several the agent can choose.
4. Planning Multiple Steps Toward An Answer

blocks.alt: Planning Multiple Steps Toward An Answer
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721032-142309857.png
Much like the multi-hop questions covered in Chain Of Thought, the agent plans a sequence of steps rather than retrieving once and stopping.
Each step's result informs what the agent decides to do next.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: An agent that retrieves once, notices the result is incomplete, then calls a second tool based on that gap is planning in the same sense as the multi-hop reasoning covered in Chain of Thought.

blocks.text: 5. The Agent Decides When Enough Information Exists

blocks.alt: The Agent Decides When Enough Information Exists
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721032-887994878.png
Much like the retrieval decision covered in Self-RAG, the agent evaluates its own gathered information and decides whether more retrieval is needed.
This replaces a fixed, predetermined number of retrieval calls.
6. Agentic Loops Can Run Too Long

blocks.alt: Agentic Loops Can Run Too Long
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721033-609943432.png
Without a hard limit on the number of steps, an agent can loop indefinitely chasing a marginal improvement.
A maximum step count keeps the loop bounded and predictable.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Safeguard","What it prevents"],"rows":[["Maximum step count","An agent looping indefinitely chasing marginal gains"],["Stopping condition on information sufficiency","Retrieving far more than the query actually needs"]]}

blocks.text: 7. Agentic RAG Builds On Modular Tools
As covered generally with routing between modules in Modular RAG, an agent's tool choices are effectively a dynamic version of that same module routing idea.
The choice is decided per step at runtime rather than fixed in advance.
8. More Autonomy Means More Unpredictability
As Advanced RAG covers, each added step costs latency, and an agent's own step by step decisions are harder to predict in advance than a fixed pipeline.
This is a real tradeoff against the flexibility that autonomy buys.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A fixed pipeline's cost and latency can be estimated in advance, while an agent's own step count varies query by query, a real unpredictability tradeoff against the flexibility autonomy provides.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Agentic RAG Earns Its Added Unpredictability

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Agentic RAG Earns Its Added Unpredictability
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447721033-493834496.png
Open-ended tasks needing several different tools suit an agentic approach.
A single, well-defined retrieval task, by contrast, rarely needs full agent autonomy.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Giving an agent tool access without a maximum step count to bound the loop.
Using full agentic autonomy for a single, well-defined retrieval task that did not need it.
Forgetting that an agent's cost and latency vary per query, unlike a fixed pipeline.
Treating tool selection as fixed in advance rather than decided dynamically at each step.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Agentic RAG lets an autonomous agent decide what to retrieve, when, and when to stop.
A fixed pipeline runs the same stages every time; an agent decides its next action per step.
An agentic system can call a web search tool, a calculator, or a database, not just a retriever.
The agent plans a sequence of steps, with each result informing the next decision.
The agent evaluates its own gathered information rather than making a fixed number of calls.
A maximum step count keeps an agentic loop bounded instead of running indefinitely.
An agent's tool choices are effectively a dynamic, runtime version of modular routing.
More autonomy trades predictable cost and latency for flexibility.
